note: Every degree name is quoted as published, and every program was verified on a first-party institutional page or a national program search. Accreditation is deliberately not evaluated here: robotics has no professional licence, so accreditation status does not gate any robotics career.

robotics_engineering.label: Robotics / robotics engineering degree
robotics_engineering.blurb: A standalone bachelor's degree whose published name is Robotics or Robotics Engineering. This is the category most people mean by “a BS in robotics”.

mechatronics.label: Mechatronics engineering degree
mechatronics.blurb: Named Mechatronics rather than Robotics. Heavily overlapping subject matter — actuators, sensors, embedded control — but a different degree title on the diploma, and usually more manufacturing-oriented.

robotics_engineering_technology.label: Engineering technology degree — not an engineering degree
robotics_engineering_technology.blurb: An applied, technician-oriented degree rather than an engineering design degree: more hands-on operation and less math and design theory. Robotics has no professional licence, so nothing legally separates these from engineering degrees — but the coursework is materially lighter on theory, which matters for AI/robotics research and graduate study.

concentration_or_track.label: Track inside another degree — not a robotics degree
concentration_or_track.blurb: The diploma says Mechanical Engineering, or similar, with robotics as a concentration, option or named track. Often excellent preparation, but it is not a robotics degree.

ai_or_cs_degree.label: AI or CS degree with robotics content
ai_or_cs_degree.blurb: A computing degree with substantial robotics coursework rather than a robotics degree.

callouts.title: Indiana University's robotics degree opens for exactly his cycle
callouts.body: IU's newsroom states: “The new degree will be available for students to apply in the fall of 2026 with the first cohort starting in the fall of 2027.” That is his year — he would be in the inaugural cohort of the Luddy School's BS in Robotics. Upside: a new program courts strong applicants. Downside: a brand-new degree has no outcomes, no alumni network and no track record, and its curriculum is still unproven.

callouts.title: CMU's BS in Robotics routes through its hardest college
callouts.body: CMU does publish a Bachelor of Science in Robotics (BSR), but its admissions page says “Submit your application for the School of Computer Science.” SCS is the ~5% college. Applying “robotics” at CMU therefore means applying to the single most selective door in the university — the opposite of a back way in.

callouts.title: Georgia Tech has no undergraduate robotics degree
callouts.body: Despite a large robotics presence, Georgia Tech's dedicated robotics degrees are graduate-only — an MS in Robotics and a PhD in Robotics. At undergraduate level the route is a mechanical engineering degree with an automation and robotics concentration.

callouts.title: The declaration gate varies enormously, and it decides whether the degree is real
callouts.body: Michigan lets students declare the Robotics BSE at a 2.0 GPA after one term in the College of Engineering. UC Santa Cruz screens at a 2.8 cumulative GPA. Minnesota State Mankato requires a separate application to the programme in sophomore year. Michigan-Dearborn direct-admits at a 3.0 high school GPA. A degree you cannot declare into is not actually available to you.
